			TokenHash: domain.HashToken(plainToken), Purpose: "reset_password",
		})
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			return ErrTokenInvalid
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		user, err := q.GetUser(ctx, row.UserID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if probs := domain.CheckPassword(newPassword, user.Email, s.breaches); len(probs) > 0 {
			return domain.PasswordRejected(probs)
		}
		hash, err := domain.HashPassword(newPassword, domain.DefaultParams())
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := q.UpdatePasswordHashTx(ctx, row.UserID, hash); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// A password change revokes EVERY session. If the reset happened
		// because the account was compromised, leaving the attacker's
		// refresh tokens alive defeats the entire exercise.
		if err := q.RevokeAllFamilies(ctx, RevokeAllFamiliesParams{
			UserID: row.UserID, Reason: "password_reset",
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// Reaching a verified address proves control of it, so a reset
		// also verifies the email if it was not already.
		if err := q.MarkEmailVerified(ctx, row.UserID); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		_, err = outbox.Enqueue(ctx, tx, "identity.password_changed",
			map[string]any{"user_id": row.UserID, "email": user.Email})
		return err
	})
}

The HTTP surface

EndpointNotes
POST/v1/auth/registerAlways 202. Never reveals whether the address exists
POST/v1/auth/verify-emailSingle-use token; idempotent on replay within the window
POST/v1/auth/loginRate limited by address and network; one generic error
POST/v1/auth/login/totpSecond step; consumes the short-lived MFA token
POST/v1/auth/password/forgotAlways 202, whatever the address
POST/v1/auth/password/resetRevokes every session on success
POST/v1/auth/refreshRotation with reuse detection — D05
POST/v1/auth/logoutRevokes this family
DELETE/v1/auth/sessionsRevokes every family — “sign out everywhere”
GET/.well-known/jwks.jsonPublic keys for the gateway — D05
services/identity/internal/transport/http/auth.go
package http

import (
	"errors"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/httpx"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/problem"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/validate"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/identity/internal/app"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/identity/internal/domain"
)

type registerRequest struct {
	Email       string `json:"email"`
	Password    string `json:"password"`
	DisplayName string `json:"display_name"`
}

func (r registerRequest) Validate() *problem.Problem {
	return validate.New().
		Required("email", r.Email).Email("email", r.Email).
		Required("password", r.Password).
		Required("display_name", r.DisplayName).
		Length("display_name", r.DisplayName, 1, 80).
		UTF8("display_name", r.DisplayName).
		Problem()
}

func (h *Handler) register(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	req, p := httpx.Decode[registerRequest](w, r)
	if p != nil {
		problem.Write(r.Context(), w, p)
		return
	}
	if p := req.Validate(); p != nil {
		problem.Write(r.Context(), w, p)
		return
	}

	_, err := h.app.Register(r.Context(), app.RegisterInput{
		Email: req.Email, Password: req.Password, DisplayName: req.DisplayName,
	})
	if err != nil {
		h.writeError(w, r, err)
		return
	}

	// 202, not 201, and no body describing what was created. The client
	// cannot tell a new registration from a duplicate, which is exactly
	// the property we want.
	httpx.JSON(r.Context(), w, http.StatusAccepted, map[string]string{
		"message": "check your email to finish signing up",
	})
}

// writeError is the single translation point from domain errors to
// problem documents. Everything not explicitly listed becomes a 500 with
// a generic body and a logged cause (B03).
func (h *Handler) writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
	ctx := r.Context()

	var pr *domain.PasswordRejectedError
	switch {
	case errors.As(err, &pr):
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Validation(pr.Fields()))
	case errors.Is(err, app.ErrInvalidCredentials):
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Unauthorized("email or password is incorrect"))
	case errors.Is(err, app.ErrTokenInvalid):
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.New(http.StatusGone, "token-invalid",
			"Link expired", "request a new one"))
	case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
		return // the client hung up; there is nobody to answer
	default:
		var p *problem.Problem
		if errors.As(err, &p) { // rate limiter and other typed problems
			problem.Write(ctx, w, p)
			return
		}
		h.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "unhandled", "err", err, "path", r.Pattern)
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Internal())
	}
}
Interview follow-up

“How would you stop someone discovering which email addresses have accounts?” Make every observable identical: the same status code, the same response body, and the same latency, on registration, login and password reset alike. The latency part is the one people miss — hashing a dummy password on the unknown-user path is what stops a stopwatch revealing the answer. Then rate limit before the lookup rather than after, so an attacker cannot infer existence from which addresses start returning 429. And accept the residual leak honestly: if signup is open, an attacker can still try to register an address and observe whether a verification email arrives.

D05

Identity II: sessions, token rotation and reuse detection

Two tokens with opposite properties: a short-lived signed access token that any service can verify with no network call, and a long-lived opaque refresh token that only identity can verify and that can be revoked instantly. Rotation plus reuse detection turns a stolen token from a permanent breach into a two-minute one. A02 builds the device and session management on top of what this chapter establishes.

Why two tokens

access token JWT, EdDSA, 10 minutes · verified LOCALLY by the gateway using cached JWKS · zero network cost per request · cannot be revoked — that is the price · so it must be short enough that the exposure window is acceptable refresh token opaque random, 32 bytes, 30 days · only identity can verify it, against a hash · revocable instantly by deleting a row · rotated on every use · presenting an already-rotated one is proof of theft The combination gives you the property neither has alone: verification with no per-request lookup, and the ability to end a session now. ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ family = one login on one device │ │ │ │ login ──▶ rt₁ ──rotate──▶ rt₂ ──rotate──▶ rt₃ ──▶ … │ │ │ │ │ └── someone presents rt₁ again ← IMPOSSIBLE │ │ unless it was copied │ │ ⇒ revoke the entire family, log out the │ │ device, and notify the user │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Reuse detection is the feature, and it is why refresh tokens must not be JWTs

A stateless JWT refresh token cannot be rotated meaningfully — there is no server-side record to mark as used, so a copied token stays valid until it expires and you have no way to know it was copied. With an opaque token and a database row you get both: rotation makes every token single-use, and a second presentation of a used token is unambiguous evidence of theft, because the legitimate client has already moved on to the next one. Revoking the whole family at that moment is what converts a stolen token from a month-long compromise into minutes.

Signing keys

services/identity/internal/domain/keys.go
package domain

import (
	"crypto/aes"
	"crypto/cipher"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/base64"
	"fmt"
)

// Ed25519 rather than RSA: 64-byte signatures instead of 256, and
// verification is fast enough that the gateway can do it inline on every
// request without it appearing in a profile.
type SigningKey struct {
	KID     string
	Public  ed25519.PublicKey
	Private ed25519.PrivateKey
}

func GenerateSigningKey() (SigningKey, error) {
	pub, priv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		return SigningKey{}, err
	}
	// The kid is derived from the public key, so it is stable, unique,
	// and reveals nothing.
	return SigningKey{KID: kidFor(pub), Public: pub, Private: priv}, nil
}

// The private half is encrypted at rest with a key from the environment
// (in production, from KMS). A database backup alone must not let anyone
// mint tokens.
func (k SigningKey) Seal(masterKey []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	block, err := aes.NewCipher(masterKey)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	gcm, err := cipher.NewGCM(block)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	nonce := make([]byte, gcm.NonceSize())
	if _, err := rand.Read(nonce); err != nil { // NEVER reuse a GCM nonce
		return nil, err
	}
	// The kid is authenticated additional data, so a sealed private key
	// cannot be moved to a different kid's row.
	return gcm.Seal(nonce, nonce, k.Private, []byte(k.KID)), nil
}

func OpenSigningKey(kid string, sealed, masterKey []byte) (ed25519.PrivateKey, error) {
	block, err := aes.NewCipher(masterKey)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	gcm, err := cipher.NewGCM(block)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(sealed) < gcm.NonceSize() {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("sealed key too short")
	}
	nonce, ct := sealed[:gcm.NonceSize()], sealed[gcm.NonceSize():]
	priv, err := gcm.Open(nil, nonce, ct, []byte(kid))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open signing key %s: %w", kid, err)
	}
	return ed25519.PrivateKey(priv), nil
}
services/identity/internal/app/jwks.go
package app

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/base64"
	"time"
)

// JWKS is the public half, served at /.well-known/jwks.json. It contains
// EVERY non-retired key, not just the active one — during rotation there
// are two, and tokens signed with the old one must keep verifying until
// they expire.
type JWK struct {
	Kty string `json:"kty"` // "OKP"
	Crv string `json:"crv"` // "Ed25519"
	Kid string `json:"kid"`
	X   string `json:"x"`   // base64url public key
	Use string `json:"use"` // "sig"
	Alg string `json:"alg"` // "EdDSA"
}

type JWKSet struct {
	Keys []JWK `json:"keys"`
}

func (s *Service) JWKS(ctx context.Context) (JWKSet, error) {
	keys, err := s.q.ListPublishableKeys(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return JWKSet{}, err
	}
	set := JWKSet{Keys: make([]JWK, 0, len(keys))}
	for _, k := range keys {
		set.Keys = append(set.Keys, JWK{
			Kty: "OKP", Crv: "Ed25519", Kid: k.Kid, Use: "sig", Alg: "EdDSA",
			X: base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(k.PublicKey),
		})
	}
	return set, nil
}

// Rotation is three steps spread over time, and the gaps matter:
//
//  1. INSERT a new key as active; the old one becomes inactive but stays
//     publishable. New tokens use the new key immediately.
//  2. Wait longer than the access-token TTL plus the gateway's JWKS
//     cache TTL — every token signed with the old key must have expired
//     AND every gateway must have refetched. 1 hour is comfortable for
//     a 10-minute token and a 5-minute cache.
//  3. Set retired_at, which removes it from the JWKS.
//
// Skipping the wait in step 2 invalidates live sessions.
func (s *Service) RotateSigningKey(ctx context.Context) error {
	k, err := domain.GenerateSigningKey()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	sealed, err := k.Seal(s.masterKey)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return pg.InTx(ctx, s.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		q := s.q.WithTx(tx)
		// The partial unique index enforces exactly one active key, so
		// this deactivate-then-insert cannot leave two or zero.
		if err := q.DeactivateAllKeys(ctx); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return q.InsertSigningKey(ctx, InsertSigningKeyParams{
			Kid: k.KID, PublicKey: k.Public, PrivateKeyEnc: sealed,
		})
	})
}

Minting the access token

services/identity/internal/app/tokens.go
package app

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/base64"
	"net/netip"
	"time"

	"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/idgen"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/identity/internal/domain"
)

const (
	accessTTL  = 10 * time.Minute
	refreshTTL = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
)

type TokenPair struct {
	AccessToken  string    `json:"access_token"`
	ExpiresAt    time.Time `json:"expires_at"`
	RefreshToken string    `json:"refresh_token"` // returned once; set as a cookie
	FamilyID     idgen.ID  `json:"-"`
}

type Claims struct {
	jwt.RegisteredClaims
	Email string `json:"email"`
	SID   string `json:"sid"` // the family id: lets a service log the session
	MFA   bool   `json:"mfa"` // did this session complete a second factor?
	Ver   int    `json:"ver"` // claims schema version, for safe evolution
}

func (s *Service) mintAccessToken(ctx context.Context, userID idgen.ID,
	email string, familyID idgen.ID, mfa bool) (string, time.Time, error) {

	key, err := s.activeKey(ctx) // cached in-process, refreshed each minute
	if err != nil {
		return "", time.Time{}, err
	}

	now := time.Now()
	exp := now.Add(accessTTL)

	tok := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodEdDSA, Claims{
		RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
			Subject:   userID.String(),
			Issuer:    s.issuer,           // verified by the gateway
			Audience:  jwt.ClaimStrings{"quill-api"},
			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(now),
			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(exp),
			// A jti lets us deny-list one specific token in an emergency
			// without revoking the whole family.
			ID: idgen.New().String(),
		},
		Email: email, SID: familyID.String(), MFA: mfa, Ver: 1,
	})
	tok.Header["kid"] = key.KID

	signed, err := tok.SignedString(key.Private)
	return signed, exp, err
}

// The refresh token is opaque randomness — no structure, no claims,
// nothing to parse. Its only meaning is "this hash exists in a row".
func newRefreshToken() (plain string, hash []byte) {
	b := make([]byte, 32)
	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
		panic("crypto/rand failed: " + err.Error())
	}
	plain = base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b)
	return plain, domain.HashToken(plain)
}

func (s *Service) issueSession(ctx context.Context, userID idgen.ID,
	userAgent string, ip netip.Prefix, mfa bool) (TokenPair, error) {

	familyID := idgen.New()
	plain, hash := newRefreshToken()

	var email string
	err := pg.InTx(ctx, s.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		q := s.q.WithTx(tx)

		u, err := q.GetUser(ctx, userID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		email = u.Email

		// Cap concurrent devices. Without a cap, a compromised account
		// can accumulate hundreds of live sessions and "log out
		// everywhere" becomes the only remedy.
		if err := q.RevokeOldestFamiliesOver(ctx, RevokeOldestFamiliesOverParams{
			UserID: userID, Keep: 10, Reason: "device_limit",
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if err := q.InsertTokenFamily(ctx, InsertTokenFamilyParams{
			ID: familyID, UserID: userID, UserAgent: truncate(userAgent, 200),
			IpPrefix: ip,
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return q.InsertRefreshToken(ctx, InsertRefreshTokenParams{
			ID: idgen.New(), FamilyID: familyID, TokenHash: hash,
			ExpiresAt: time.Now().Add(refreshTTL),
		})
	})
	if err != nil {
		return TokenPair{}, err
	}

	access, exp, err := s.mintAccessToken(ctx, userID, email, familyID, mfa)
	if err != nil {
		return TokenPair{}, err
	}
	return TokenPair{AccessToken: access, ExpiresAt: exp,
		RefreshToken: plain, FamilyID: familyID}, nil
}

Rotation, with reuse detection

services/identity/internal/app/refresh.go
package app

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/netip"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/outbox"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/pg"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/identity/internal/domain"
)

var (
	ErrRefreshInvalid = errors.New("refresh token is invalid or expired")
	ErrTokenReuse     = errors.New("refresh token reuse detected")
)

func (s *Service) Refresh(ctx context.Context, plain string,
	userAgent string, ip netip.Prefix) (TokenPair, error) {

	hash := domain.HashToken(plain)
	var out TokenPair

	err := pg.InTx(ctx, s.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		q := s.q.WithTx(tx)

		// SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the family row serialises concurrent
		// refreshes from the same device. Without it, two tabs refreshing
		// simultaneously both "win" and one of them then looks like reuse
		// — a self-inflicted logout that is maddening to debug.
		row, err := q.FindRefreshTokenForUpdate(ctx, hash)
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			return ErrRefreshInvalid
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// ── the reuse branch ──────────────────────────────────────────
		// This token was already rotated. The legitimate client has moved
		// on, so whoever presented this copied it. We cannot tell which
		// party is the attacker, so we revoke everything and force a
		// fresh login — inconvenient, and unambiguously correct.
		if row.UsedAt.Valid {
			if err := q.RevokeFamily(ctx, RevokeFamilyParams{
				ID: row.FamilyID, Reason: "token_reuse",
			}); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if _, err := outbox.Enqueue(ctx, tx, "identity.token_reuse_detected",
				map[string]any{
					"user_id": row.UserID, "family_id": row.FamilyID,
					"ip": ip.String(), "user_agent": userAgent,
				}); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh token reuse",
				"user_id", row.UserID, "family_id", row.FamilyID)
			tokenReuseTotal.Inc() // alert on this: it is a real signal
			return ErrTokenReuse
		}

		if row.FamilyRevokedAt.Valid {
			return ErrRefreshInvalid
		}
		if time.Now().After(row.ExpiresAt) {
			return ErrRefreshInvalid
		}

		// ── the normal branch: rotate ─────────────────────────────────
		newPlain, newHash := newRefreshToken()
		newID := idgen.New()

		if err := q.InsertRefreshToken(ctx, InsertRefreshTokenParams{
			ID: newID, FamilyID: row.FamilyID, TokenHash: newHash,
			// The new token inherits the family's ORIGINAL expiry rather
			// than extending it. Otherwise a session refreshed daily
			// never ends, and "30-day sessions" becomes "forever".
			ExpiresAt: row.FamilyExpiresAt,
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		// Mark the old one used and link it, so the chain is auditable.
		if err := q.MarkRefreshTokenUsed(ctx, MarkRefreshTokenUsedParams{
			ID: row.ID, ReplacedBy: newID,
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := q.TouchFamily(ctx, TouchFamilyParams{
			ID: row.FamilyID, UserAgent: truncate(userAgent, 200), IpPrefix: ip,
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		access, exp, err := s.mintAccessToken(ctx, row.UserID, row.Email,
			row.FamilyID, row.MFA)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		out = TokenPair{AccessToken: access, ExpiresAt: exp,
			RefreshToken: newPlain, FamilyID: row.FamilyID}
		return nil
	})
	return out, err
}
services/identity/query.sql — the refresh queries
-- name: FindRefreshTokenForUpdate :one
-- The FOR UPDATE is on token_families, not refresh_tokens: it serialises
-- every refresh for this device, which is what makes concurrent tabs
-- safe. Locking the token row instead would not, because the second
-- request reads a DIFFERENT row (the one just created).
SELECT rt.id, rt.family_id, rt.token_hash, rt.expires_at, rt.used_at,
       f.user_id, f.revoked_at AS family_revoked_at,
       f.created_at + interval '30 days' AS family_expires_at,
       u.email
  FROM refresh_tokens rt
  JOIN token_families f ON f.id = rt.family_id
  JOIN users u          ON u.id = f.user_id
 WHERE rt.token_hash = @token_hash
   FOR UPDATE OF f;

-- name: MarkRefreshTokenUsed :exec
UPDATE refresh_tokens SET used_at = now(), replaced_by = @replaced_by
 WHERE id = @id AND used_at IS NULL;

-- name: RevokeFamily :exec
UPDATE token_families SET revoked_at = now(), revoked_reason = @reason
 WHERE id = @id AND revoked_at IS NULL;

-- name: RevokeOldestFamiliesOver :exec
-- Keep the N most recently used sessions, revoke the rest.
UPDATE token_families SET revoked_at = now(), revoked_reason = @reason
 WHERE user_id = @user_id AND revoked_at IS NULL
   AND id NOT IN (
       SELECT id FROM token_families
        WHERE user_id = @user_id AND revoked_at IS NULL
        ORDER BY last_used_at DESC
        LIMIT @keep
   );

-- name: PurgeExpiredTokens :execrows
-- Run hourly. Without it refresh_tokens grows forever — every rotation
-- adds a row, so an active user generates ~4000 a month.
DELETE FROM refresh_tokens
 WHERE expires_at < now() - interval '7 days';
The concurrent-refresh problem is real and it will page you

A browser with three tabs, or a client that fires two requests as the access token expires, produces two simultaneous refreshes with the same token. Without serialisation both read an unused token, both rotate, and one of them becomes a “reuse” on its next attempt — logging the user out for no reason. The row lock above fixes it: the second request blocks, then finds the token already used and correctly reports reuse only if it is a genuinely stale token. An alternative some systems use is a short grace window where the immediately-previous token still works; the lock is simpler and does not weaken the guarantee.

Where the tokens live on the client

ClientAccess tokenRefresh token
BrowserIn memory only — never localStorage, which any XSS can readHttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /v1/auth/refresh
Desktop / syncdIn memoryOS keychain, or a file with mode 0600 in the user's config directory
MobileIn memoryKeychain / Keystore
services/identity/internal/transport/http/cookies.go
package http

import (
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

const refreshCookie = "quill_rt"

func setRefreshCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, token string, ttl time.Duration, prod bool) {
	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
		Name:  refreshCookie,
		Value: token,
		// Scoped to the ONE endpoint that needs it. A cookie on "/" is
		// sent with every request including static assets, which is both
		// wasteful and a larger attack surface.
		Path:     "/v1/auth/refresh",
		MaxAge:   int(ttl.Seconds()),
		HttpOnly: true,                    // JavaScript cannot read it → XSS
		Secure:   prod,                    // HTTPS only
		SameSite: http.SameSiteStrictMode, // CSRF: never sent cross-site
	})
}

func clearRefreshCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, prod bool) {
	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
		Name: refreshCookie, Value: "", Path: "/v1/auth/refresh",
		MaxAge: -1, HttpOnly: true, Secure: prod, SameSite: http.SameSiteStrictMode,
	})
}

func (h *Handler) refresh(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	// Accept the token from the cookie (browser) or the body (native
	// clients, which have no cookie jar). Never from a query string:
	// URLs end up in access logs, browser history and Referer headers.
	token := ""
	if c, err := r.Cookie(refreshCookie); err == nil {
		token = c.Value
	}
	if token == "" {
		req, p := httpx.Decode[struct {
			RefreshToken string `json:"refresh_token"`
		}](w, r)
		if p != nil {
			problem.Write(r.Context(), w, p)
			return
		}
		token = req.RefreshToken
	}
	if token == "" {
		problem.Write(r.Context(), w, problem.Unauthorized("no refresh token"))
		return
	}

	pair, err := h.app.Refresh(r.Context(), token, r.UserAgent(), clientPrefix(r))
	if err != nil {
		// On reuse, clear the cookie too — the legitimate user's browser
		// should stop presenting a token that is now poison.
		if errors.Is(err, app.ErrTokenReuse) {
			clearRefreshCookie(w, h.prod)
			problem.Write(r.Context(), w, problem.New(http.StatusUnauthorized,
				"session-revoked", "Session ended",
				"your session was ended for security reasons; please sign in again"))
			return
		}
		h.writeError(w, r, err)
		return
	}

	setRefreshCookie(w, pair.RefreshToken, refreshTTL, h.prod)
	pair.RefreshToken = "" // do not ALSO put it in the body for browsers
	httpx.JSON(r.Context(), w, http.StatusOK, pair)
}

TOTP

services/identity/internal/app/totp.go
package app

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/subtle"
	"errors"
	"time"

	"github.com/pquerna/otp/totp"
)

// Enrolment is two steps on purpose: generating a secret does not enable
// 2FA. The user must prove they can produce a code first, or a mistyped
// QR scan locks them out permanently.
func (s *Service) BeginTOTPEnrolment(ctx context.Context, userID idgen.ID) (string, string, error) {
	u, err := s.q.GetUser(ctx, userID)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	key, err := totp.Generate(totp.GenerateOpts{
		Issuer: "Quill", AccountName: u.Email, Period: 30, Digits: 6,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	enc, err := domain.SealSecret([]byte(key.Secret()), s.masterKey)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	// confirmed_at stays NULL: 2FA is not active yet.
	if err := s.q.UpsertUnconfirmedTOTP(ctx, userID, enc); err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	return key.Secret(), key.URL(), nil
}

func (s *Service) ConfirmTOTPEnrolment(ctx context.Context, userID idgen.ID,
	code string) ([]string, error) {

	secret, err := s.totpSecret(ctx, userID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !totp.Validate(code, secret) {
		return nil, ErrInvalidCredentials
	}

	// Recovery codes, generated once and shown once. Stored hashed, for
	// the same reason passwords are.
	plain, hashes := domain.NewRecoveryCodes(10)
	if err := s.q.ConfirmTOTP(ctx, ConfirmTOTPParams{
		UserID: userID, RecoveryHashes: hashes,
	}); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return plain, nil
}

func (s *Service) verifyTOTP(ctx context.Context, userID idgen.ID, code string) error {
	// Rate limit the code check itself. Six digits is a million
	// possibilities and a 30-second window — without a limit that is
	// brute-forceable in hours.
	if err := s.limiter.Check(ctx, "totp:"+userID.String(), 5, time.Minute); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	secret, err := s.totpSecret(ctx, userID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Skew of ±1 period tolerates clock drift. Larger windows widen the
	// replay opportunity for a code shoulder-surfed or phished.
	valid, err := totp.ValidateCustom(code, secret, time.Now(), totp.ValidateOpts{
		Period: 30, Skew: 1, Digits: 6,
	})
	if err != nil || !valid {
		return s.tryRecoveryCode(ctx, userID, code)
	}

	// A TOTP code is single-use: without this, a code captured by a
	// phishing proxy can be replayed for the remaining ~30 seconds.
	if !s.markCodeUsed(ctx, userID, code) {
		return ErrInvalidCredentials
	}
	return nil
}

Session management for the user

EndpointEffect
GET/v1/auth/sessionsLists live families with device, coarse location and last-used time
DELETE/v1/auth/sessions/{id}Revokes one device
DELETE/v1/auth/sessionsRevokes all but the current one
POST/v1/auth/totp/beginReturns the secret and otpauth:// URL; does not enable 2FA
POST/v1/auth/totp/confirmEnables it and returns ten recovery codes, once
DELETE/v1/auth/totpRequires the password and a current code
Revocation reaches an access token within its TTL, not instantly

Revoking a family kills the refresh token immediately, but an access token already in the wild stays valid until it expires — up to ten minutes. That is the trade you accepted in exchange for stateless verification, and for most products it is fine. When it is not — a compromised account, an offboarded employee — add a small Redis deny-list of revoked sid values that the gateway consults, with a TTL equal to the access-token lifetime. It costs one Redis lookup per request but only for the window that matters, and the set stays tiny because entries expire on their own.

Interview follow-up

“How do you revoke a JWT?” You cannot, which is the point of the design — verification involves no server. So you make the access token short-lived enough that the exposure window is acceptable, and you put the revocable state in an opaque refresh token backed by a database row. Then add the part most answers miss: rotate the refresh token on every use, and treat a second presentation of an already-rotated token as proof of theft, revoking the whole session family. That converts a stolen refresh token from a month of access into minutes, and it gives you a genuine security signal to alert on.

D06

The gateway

One public surface in front of six private services. It verifies tokens locally, forwards a signed identity inward, enforces the limits that must be global, and translates every failure into one error shape. It owns no data, which is what lets it be stateless and disposable.

What belongs here, and what does not

In the gatewayNot in the gateway
TLS termination, HTTP/2, compressionBusiness rules of any kind
Access-token verification (local, via cached JWKS)Issuing tokens — that is identity's job
Global rate limits and per-tenant quotasPer-resource authorization — the owning service decides
Request id, tracing, structured access logsA database connection
CORS, CSRF, security headersResponse transformation that hides a service's contract
Timeouts, retries, circuit breakers per upstreamCaching anything user-specific
Public pages (/p/{slug}) with edge cachingAggregating three services into one response by default
The failure mode to avoid: a gateway that becomes a monolith

Every team eventually wants “just one small transformation” in the gateway, and within a year it contains business logic, knows every service's schema, and must be redeployed for any change anywhere — a distributed monolith with a single point of failure at the front. The rule that prevents it: the gateway may route, verify, limit and translate, and nothing else. If a change requires knowing what a notebook is, it belongs in the notes service.

Verifying the token

platform/authn/verifier.go
// Package authn verifies Quill access tokens against the JWKS published
// by identity. It caches keys in process, so the hot path makes NO
// network call — which is the entire reason for using a signed token.
package authn

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
	"golang.org/x/sync/singleflight"
)

type Verifier struct {
	jwksURL  string
	issuer   string
	audience string
	client   *http.Client

	mu      sync.RWMutex
	keys    map[string]ed25519.PublicKey
	fetched time.Time
	group   singleflight.Group // collapse concurrent refreshes into one

	ttl       time.Duration // how long a good fetch is trusted
	staleFor  time.Duration // how long a stale set is still usable
}

func NewVerifier(jwksURL, issuer, audience string) *Verifier {
	return &Verifier{
		jwksURL: jwksURL, issuer: issuer, audience: audience,
		client:   &http.Client{Timeout: 3 * time.Second},
		keys:     map[string]ed25519.PublicKey{},
		ttl:      5 * time.Minute,
		staleFor: 24 * time.Hour,
	}
}

var (
	ErrNoToken      = errors.New("no token")
	ErrTokenInvalid = errors.New("token invalid")
	ErrKeyUnknown   = errors.New("unknown signing key")
)

func (v *Verifier) Verify(ctx context.Context, raw string) (*Claims, error) {
	var claims Claims

	tok, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(raw, &claims,
		func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) {
			// CRITICAL: pin the algorithm. Without this an attacker can
			// present alg:"none", or hand us an HMAC token signed with a
			// key we published — algorithm confusion (B10).
			if _, ok := t.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodEd25519); !ok {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected alg %v", t.Header["alg"])
			}
			kid, _ := t.Header["kid"].(string)
			if kid == "" {
				return nil, ErrKeyUnknown
			}
			return v.key(ctx, kid)
		},
		jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"EdDSA"}), // belt and braces
		jwt.WithIssuer(v.issuer),
		jwt.WithAudience(v.audience),
		jwt.WithExpirationRequired(),
		jwt.WithLeeway(30*time.Second), // clock skew between pods
	)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrTokenInvalid, err)
	}
	if !tok.Valid {
		return nil, ErrTokenInvalid
	}
	if claims.Ver != 1 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unsupported claims version %d", ErrTokenInvalid, claims.Ver)
	}
	return &claims, nil
}

func (v *Verifier) key(ctx context.Context, kid string) (ed25519.PublicKey, error) {
	v.mu.RLock()
	k, ok := v.keys[kid]
	fresh := time.Since(v.fetched) < v.ttl
	v.mu.RUnlock()

	if ok && fresh {
		return k, nil
	}
	// An unknown kid usually means identity rotated: refetch once.
	// singleflight means a thousand concurrent requests cause ONE fetch,
	// not a thundering herd against identity (L14).
	if _, err, _ := v.group.Do("jwks", func() (any, error) {
		return nil, v.refresh(ctx)
	}); err != nil {
		// Serve STALE keys rather than failing every request when
		// identity is briefly unreachable. Availability here matters
		// more than freshness, because keys change roughly never.
		v.mu.RLock()
		k, ok = v.keys[kid]
		usable := time.Since(v.fetched) < v.staleFor
		v.mu.RUnlock()
		if ok && usable {
			jwksStale.Inc()
			return k, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}

	v.mu.RLock()
	k, ok = v.keys[kid]
	v.mu.RUnlock()
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrKeyUnknown, kid)
	}
	return k, nil
}

func (v *Verifier) refresh(ctx context.Context) error {
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, v.jwksURL, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	resp, err := v.client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("fetch jwks: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() {
		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4<<10))
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
	}()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return fmt.Errorf("fetch jwks: status %d", resp.StatusCode)
	}

	var set struct {
		Keys []struct{ Kid, Kty, Crv, X string } `json:"keys"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 64<<10)).Decode(&set); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("decode jwks: %w", err)
	}

	next := make(map[string]ed25519.PublicKey, len(set.Keys))
	for _, k := range set.Keys {
		if k.Kty != "OKP" || k.Crv != "Ed25519" {
			continue
		}
		b, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(k.X)
		if err != nil || len(b) != ed25519.PublicKeySize {
			continue
		}
		next[k.Kid] = ed25519.PublicKey(b)
	}
	if len(next) == 0 {
		return errors.New("jwks contained no usable keys")
	}

	v.mu.Lock()
	v.keys, v.fetched = next, time.Now()
	v.mu.Unlock()
	return nil
}
Three decisions in that cache that matter more than they look

singleflight so a key rotation does not cause every in-flight request to hammer identity simultaneously. Stale-while-unreachable, because signing keys change roughly never and returning 401 to every user when identity is restarting is a self-inflicted outage. And refetch on unknown kid, which is what makes rotation seamless — the first token signed with a new key triggers exactly one fetch and everything continues.

The middleware chain

services/gateway/internal/transport/http/router.go
package http

import (
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/httpx"
)

func (g *Gateway) Routes() http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	// ── public, unauthenticated ──────────────────────────────────────
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/register",        g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/login",           g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/login/totp",      g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/refresh",         g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/verify-email",    g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/password/forgot", g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/auth/password/reset",  g.proxy(g.identity))
	mux.Handle("GET /.well-known/jwks.json",    g.proxy(g.identity))

	// Public note pages: no auth, aggressive caching, its own handler
	// because the response is HTML rather than JSON.
	mux.Handle("GET /p/{slug}", g.publicPage())

	// ── authenticated ────────────────────────────────────────────────
	authed := func(h http.Handler) http.Handler {
		return Chain(h, g.requireAuth, g.perUserRateLimit)
	}

	mux.Handle("GET /v1/notebooks",             authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/notebooks",            authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/notebooks/{id}",        authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("PATCH /v1/notebooks/{id}",      authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("DELETE /v1/notebooks/{id}",     authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/notebooks/{id}/notes",  authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/notes",                authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/notes/{id}",            authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("PATCH /v1/notes/{id}",          authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("DELETE /v1/notes/{id}",         authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/notes/{id}/publish",   authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("DELETE /v1/notes/{id}/publish", authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/search",                authed(g.proxy(g.notes)))

	// Sync gets its own limiter: a client draining a month of offline
	// work must not be throttled by the same budget as interactive reads.
	sync := func(h http.Handler) http.Handler {
		return Chain(h, g.requireAuth, g.syncRateLimit)
	}
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/sync/changes", sync(g.proxy(g.notes)))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/sync/push",   sync(g.proxy(g.notes)))

	mux.Handle("POST /v1/notebooks/{id}/invitations",   authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/notebooks/{id}/invitations",    authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))
	mux.Handle("DELETE /v1/invitations/{id}",           authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))
	mux.Handle("POST /v1/invitations/accept",           authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))
	mux.Handle("GET /v1/notebooks/{id}/members",        authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))
	mux.Handle("PATCH /v1/notebooks/{id}/members/{uid}", authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))
	mux.Handle("DELETE /v1/notebooks/{id}/members/{uid}", authed(g.proxy(g.collab)))

	mux.Handle("GET /v1/realtime", sync(g.websocket()))

	// Outermost first. Recoverer must wrap everything, or a panic
	// bypasses the access log entirely (B02).
	return Chain(mux,
		g.recoverer,
		g.requestID,
		g.tracing,
		g.accessLog,
		g.metrics,
		g.securityHeaders,
		g.cors,
		g.globalRateLimit,
		g.timeout(15*time.Second),
	)
}

Authentication middleware, and the internal identity header

services/gateway/internal/transport/http/auth.go
package http

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/authn"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/httpx"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/problem"
)

func (g *Gateway) requireAuth(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		ctx := r.Context()

		raw, ok := strings.CutPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")
		if !ok || raw == "" {
			problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Unauthorized("a bearer token is required"))
			return
		}

		claims, err := g.verifier.Verify(ctx, raw)
		if err != nil {
			// Never echo the parse error: it tells an attacker exactly
			// which check failed and how to get closer.
			g.log.DebugContext(ctx, "token rejected", "err", err)
			problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Unauthorized("token is invalid or expired"))
			return
		}

		// The emergency deny-list: revoked session ids, with a TTL equal
		// to the access-token lifetime so the set stays tiny. One Redis
		// GET, only on authenticated routes.
		if g.denylist != nil && g.denylist.Contains(ctx, claims.SID) {
			problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Unauthorized("session has been revoked"))
			return
		}

		sub := httpx.Subject{
			UserID: idgen.ID(claims.Subject), SessionID: idgen.ID(claims.SID),
			Email: claims.Email, MFA: claims.MFA,
		}
		ctx = httpx.WithSubject(ctx, sub)
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
	})
}

// The identity passed inward is SIGNED. Upstream services trust the
// header only if the HMAC verifies, so a pod that somehow receives
// traffic bypassing the gateway cannot be told "you are user X" by the
// caller. It is cheap defence against a misrouted ingress or a
// compromised sidecar — not a substitute for network policy.
type internalSubject struct {
	UserID string `json:"u"`
	SID    string `json:"s"`
	Email  string `json:"e"`
	MFA    bool   `json:"m"`
	Exp    int64  `json:"x"`
}

func (g *Gateway) signSubject(s httpx.Subject) string {
	payload, _ := json.Marshal(internalSubject{
		UserID: s.UserID.String(), SID: s.SessionID.String(),
		Email: s.Email, MFA: s.MFA,
		// Short expiry so a captured header cannot be replayed later.
		Exp: time.Now().Add(30 * time.Second).Unix(),
	})
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, g.internalKey)
	mac.Write(payload)
	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(payload) + "." +
		base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
}

// VerifyInternalSubject lives in platform/authn and every service calls
// it in its own middleware — services do not trust the network.
func VerifyInternalSubject(header string, key []byte) (httpx.Subject, error) {
	payloadB64, macB64, ok := strings.Cut(header, ".")
	if !ok {
		return httpx.Subject{}, ErrTokenInvalid
	}
	payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(payloadB64)
	if err != nil {
		return httpx.Subject{}, ErrTokenInvalid
	}
	want, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(macB64)
	if err != nil {
		return httpx.Subject{}, ErrTokenInvalid
	}
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
	mac.Write(payload)
	if !hmac.Equal(mac.Sum(nil), want) { // constant time
		return httpx.Subject{}, ErrTokenInvalid
	}

	var s internalSubject
	if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &s); err != nil {
		return httpx.Subject{}, ErrTokenInvalid
	}
	if time.Now().Unix() > s.Exp {
		return httpx.Subject{}, ErrTokenInvalid
	}
	return httpx.Subject{
		UserID: idgen.ID(s.UserID), SessionID: idgen.ID(s.SID),
		Email: s.Email, MFA: s.MFA,
	}, nil
}

The reverse proxy, with timeouts and a breaker

services/gateway/internal/transport/http/proxy.go
package http

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httputil"
	"net/url"
	"time"

	"github.com/sony/gobreaker/v2"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/httpx"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/problem"
)

type upstream struct {
	name    string
	proxy   *httputil.ReverseProxy
	breaker *gobreaker.CircuitBreaker[any]
}

func (g *Gateway) newUpstream(name, target string) *upstream {
	u, err := url.Parse(target)
	if err != nil {
		panic("gateway: bad upstream " + target + ": " + err.Error())
	}

	transport := &http.Transport{
		DialContext: (&net.Dialer{
			Timeout: 2 * time.Second, KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second,
		}).DialContext,
		// The default of 2 idle connections per host means a busy
		// gateway reopens TCP constantly (B11).
		MaxIdleConns:        400,
		MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 200,
		MaxConnsPerHost:     300, // a ceiling, so we cannot flood a service
		IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
		ForceAttemptHTTP2:   true,
	}

	up := &upstream{name: name}
	up.proxy = &httputil.ReverseProxy{
		Transport: transport,
		Rewrite: func(pr *httputil.ProxyRequest) {
			pr.SetURL(u)
			// SetXForwarded REPLACES any client-supplied X-Forwarded-For
			// rather than appending to it — otherwise a caller can forge
			// an origin IP and defeat IP-based limiting.
			pr.SetXForwarded()
			pr.Out.Host = pr.In.Host

			pr.Out.Header.Set("X-Request-Id", httpx.RequestID(pr.In.Context()))
			if s, ok := httpx.SubjectFrom(pr.In.Context()); ok {
				pr.Out.Header.Set("X-Quill-Subject", g.signSubject(s))
			} else {
				// Strip it explicitly: a client must never be able to
				// supply this header itself.
				pr.Out.Header.Del("X-Quill-Subject")
			}
		},
		ModifyResponse: func(resp *http.Response) error {
			// Upstreams are internal; their cache headers are not ours
			// to publish, and an accidental `Cache-Control: public` on a
			// user's notes would be a data leak through a shared cache.
			if resp.Header.Get("Cache-Control") == "" {
				resp.Header.Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
			}
			return nil
		},
		ErrorHandler: func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
			ctx := r.Context()
			switch {
			case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
				return // client hung up; nobody to answer
			case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
				problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.New(http.StatusGatewayTimeout,
					"upstream-timeout", "Upstream timed out", name+" did not respond"))
			default:
				g.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "upstream failure",
					"upstream", name, "err", err)
				problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.New(http.StatusBadGateway,
					"upstream-unavailable", "Service unavailable",
					name+" is not reachable"))
			}
		},
	}

	up.breaker = gobreaker.NewCircuitBreaker[any](gobreaker.Settings{
		Name:        name,
		MaxRequests: 5,                // probes allowed while half-open
		Interval:    60 * time.Second,
		Timeout:     20 * time.Second, // how long to stay open
		ReadyToTrip: func(c gobreaker.Counts) bool {
			// A RATE over a window, not a raw count: "5 failures" trips
			// on a quiet service after five requests (P04).
			return c.Requests >= 20 &&
				float64(c.TotalFailures)/float64(c.Requests) >= 0.5
		},
		OnStateChange: func(_ string, from, to gobreaker.State) {
			g.log.Warn("breaker", "upstream", name, "from", from, "to", to)
			breakerState.WithLabelValues(name).Set(float64(to))
		},
	})
	return up
}

func (g *Gateway) proxy(up *upstream) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		_, err := up.breaker.Execute(func() (any, error) {
			rec := &statusRecorder{ResponseWriter: w}
			up.proxy.ServeHTTP(rec, r)
			// Only 5xx counts as a breaker failure. A 404 or a 422 is the
			// service working correctly and must not trip anything.
			if rec.status >= 500 {
				return nil, errUpstream
			}
			return nil, nil
		})
		if errors.Is(err, gobreaker.ErrOpenState) {
			// Fail fast rather than waiting for a timeout on something
			// we already know is down.
			w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "20")
			problem.Write(r.Context(), w, problem.New(http.StatusServiceUnavailable,
				"upstream-unavailable", "Service unavailable",
				up.name+" is temporarily unavailable"))
		}
	})
}
Only 5xx may trip a circuit breaker

Counting every non-2xx as a failure means a burst of legitimate 404s or validation 422s opens the breaker and takes a healthy service offline — which is a genuinely spectacular way to cause an outage from correct behaviour. A breaker measures whether the dependency is broken, not whether requests are succeeding. The same distinction governs retries: a 4xx is never retryable because repeating it cannot help.

Rate limiting at three scopes

services/gateway/internal/transport/http/ratelimit.go
package http

// Three scopes, three purposes. Getting these confused produces either a
// gateway that lets one tenant starve everyone else, or one that blocks
// a legitimate user syncing a month of offline edits.
func (g *Gateway) globalRateLimit(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		// Per network prefix, for UNAUTHENTICATED traffic. Its job is
		// brute-force and scraping defence, not fairness.
		key := "gw:ip:" + clientPrefix(r).String()
		if err := g.limiter.Check(r.Context(), key, 300, time.Minute); err != nil {
			g.writeLimited(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

func (g *Gateway) perUserRateLimit(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		// Per authenticated principal, for FAIRNESS. IP-based limiting
		// punishes everyone behind one NAT and is trivially evaded by
		// anyone who matters (B09).
		s := httpx.MustSubject(r.Context())
		if err := g.limiter.Check(r.Context(), "gw:user:"+s.UserID.String(),
			600, time.Minute); err != nil {
			g.writeLimited(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

func (g *Gateway) syncRateLimit(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		// A separate, much larger budget. A client returning after a
		// month offline legitimately makes hundreds of calls in a
		// minute, and throttling it into failure is how "sync is broken"
		// bug reports are born.
		s := httpx.MustSubject(r.Context())
		if err := g.limiter.Check(r.Context(), "gw:sync:"+s.UserID.String(),
			3000, time.Minute); err != nil {
			g.writeLimited(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

func (g *Gateway) writeLimited(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
	// Always tell the client WHEN to come back. A 429 with no
	// Retry-After teaches clients to retry immediately, which turns a
	// rate limit into a retry storm.
	w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "5")
	rateLimited.WithLabelValues(r.Pattern).Inc()
	problem.Write(r.Context(), w, problem.TooManyRequests(5))
}

CORS, CSRF and security headers

services/gateway/internal/transport/http/security.go
package http

func (g *Gateway) cors(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		origin := r.Header.Get("Origin")
		if origin != "" {
			if _, allowed := g.allowedOrigins[origin]; allowed {
				w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
				w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", "true")
				w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Headers",
					"Authorization, Content-Type, X-Request-Id, X-CSRF-Token")
				w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Methods",
					"GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS")
				w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Max-Age", "600")
			}
			// Vary ALWAYS, allowed or not — otherwise a shared cache
			// serves one origin's CORS response to another (P06).
			w.Header().Add("Vary", "Origin")
		}
		if r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
			return
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

// CSRF applies ONLY to the cookie-authenticated endpoint — the refresh
// route. Everything else uses a bearer token, which a cross-site form
// post cannot attach, so those routes need no token.
func (g *Gateway) csrf(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead {
			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
			return
		}
		// Double-submit: the cookie and the header must match. SameSite
		// =Strict on the refresh cookie already blocks this, but defence
		// in depth costs nothing and covers older browsers.
		c, err := r.Cookie("quill_csrf")
		if err != nil || c.Value == "" ||
			subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(c.Value),
				[]byte(r.Header.Get("X-CSRF-Token"))) != 1 {
			problem.Write(r.Context(), w, problem.Forbidden("csrf token mismatch"))
			return
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

func (g *Gateway) securityHeaders(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		h := w.Header()
		h.Set("Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains")
		h.Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
		h.Set("X-Frame-Options", "DENY")
		h.Set("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin")
		h.Set("Permissions-Policy", "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()")
		// The API returns JSON, so the strictest possible CSP applies.
		// The public note page sets its own, looser, policy.
		h.Set("Content-Security-Policy",
			"default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'")
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

Wiring it up

services/gateway/cmd/api/main.go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/redis/go-redis/v9"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/authn"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/config"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/httpx"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/obs"
	gwhttp "github.com/quillhq/quill/services/gateway/internal/transport/http"
)

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		slog.Error("fatal", "err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func run() error {
	cfg, err := loadConfig()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	log := obs.NewLogger(cfg.Base)
	log.Info("starting",
		"gomaxprocs", runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0),      // verify the tuning (P03)
		"gomemlimit", debug.SetMemoryLimit(-1))

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(),
		os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()

	shutdownTracing, err := obs.InitTracing(ctx, cfg.Base)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() {
		sc, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		_ = shutdownTracing(sc) // flush the last spans or you lose them
	}()

	rdb := redis.NewClient(&redis.Options{
		Addr: cfg.RedisAddr, PoolSize: 40, MinIdleConns: 10,
		DialTimeout:  2 * time.Second,
		ReadTimeout:  200 * time.Millisecond, // a slow limiter is worse
		WriteTimeout: 200 * time.Millisecond, // than no limiter
	})
	defer rdb.Close()

	gw := gwhttp.New(gwhttp.Options{
		Log:            log,
		Verifier:       authn.NewVerifier(cfg.JWKSURL, cfg.Issuer, "quill-api"),
		Limiter:        authn.NewLimiter(rdb),
		Denylist:       authn.NewDenylist(rdb),
		InternalKey:    []byte(cfg.InternalSigningKey.Reveal()),
		AllowedOrigins: cfg.AllowedOrigins,
		Upstreams: map[string]string{
			"identity": cfg.IdentityURL,
			"notes":    cfg.NotesURL,
			"collab":   cfg.CollabURL,
			"realtime": cfg.RealtimeURL,
		},
	})

	srv := httpx.NewServer(httpx.Options{
		Addr:            cfg.Addr,
		InternalAddr:    cfg.InternalAddr,
		Handler:         gw.Routes(),
		Log:             log,
		ShutdownTimeout: cfg.ShutdownTimeout,
		// The gateway is ready if it can reach Redis. It deliberately
		// does NOT check upstreams: a notes outage must not remove the
		// gateway from the load balancer and take auth down with it.
		ReadinessCheck: func(ctx context.Context) error { return rdb.Ping(ctx).Err() },
	})

	return srv.Run(ctx)
}
Readiness should reflect what this pod cannot do without

A gateway that fails readiness when the notes service is down removes itself from the load balancer, so login and public pages — which do not need notes at all — stop working too. One service's degradation becomes a total outage. Check only the dependencies whose absence makes every route fail, and let the circuit breakers handle the rest by returning 503 for the affected routes while the others keep serving.

Interview follow-up

“Why put an API gateway in front of services rather than exposing them directly?” One public TLS surface and one CORS policy instead of six; token verification implemented once rather than copied; global rate limits that actually work because they see all traffic; and a single place to translate failures into one error shape. Then name the danger, because that is what an interviewer is listening for: a gateway accumulates logic until it is a monolith with a single point of failure at the front. The rule that prevents it is that the gateway may route, verify, limit and translate, and must never know what a domain object is.

D07

The notes service: domain, storage and the write path

The core service. This chapter builds the domain types with their rules, the sqlc-backed store, the use-case layer, and the write path that produces both a row update and an operation-log entry in one transaction — because every write here is also a sync event.

The domain, which imports nothing

services/notes/internal/domain/note.go
// Package domain holds the types and the rules. It imports the standard
// library and platform/idgen, and nothing else — no database, no HTTP,
// no framework. That is what makes these rules unit-testable in
// microseconds and reusable from the sync path and the REST path alike.
package domain

import (
	"errors"
	"strings"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/idgen"
)

type Visibility string

const (
	Private Visibility = "private" // only members of the notebook
	Shared  Visibility = "shared"  // members, and explicitly granted users
	Public  Visibility = "public"  // anyone with the link
)

func (v Visibility) Valid() bool {
	switch v {
	case Private, Shared, Public:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

type Role string

const (
	RoleOwner     Role = "owner"
	RoleEditor    Role = "editor"
	RoleCommenter Role = "commenter"
	RoleViewer    Role = "viewer"
)

// rank orders roles so a comparison replaces a chain of equality checks.
// Keeping it unexported means callers must use the Can* methods, which
// is what stops "role == editor" appearing in forty places.
var rank = map[Role]int{RoleViewer: 1, RoleCommenter: 2, RoleEditor: 3, RoleOwner: 4}

func (r Role) atLeast(min Role) bool { return rank[r] >= rank[min] }

func (r Role) CanRead() bool    { return r.atLeast(RoleViewer) }
func (r Role) CanComment() bool { return r.atLeast(RoleCommenter) }
func (r Role) CanWrite() bool   { return r.atLeast(RoleEditor) }
func (r Role) CanShare() bool   { return r.atLeast(RoleOwner) }
func (r Role) CanPublish() bool { return r.atLeast(RoleOwner) }
func (r Role) CanDelete() bool  { return r.atLeast(RoleOwner) }

const (
	MaxTitleRunes = 200
	MaxBodyBytes  = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB — bounded so one note cannot OOM a pod
)

var (
	ErrNotFound      = errors.New("note not found")
	ErrNotebookGone  = errors.New("notebook not found")
	ErrForbidden     = errors.New("not permitted")
	ErrVersionStale  = errors.New("note was modified by someone else")
	ErrTitleTooLong  = errors.New("title is too long")
	ErrBodyTooLarge  = errors.New("body is too large")
	ErrBadVisibility = errors.New("invalid visibility")
)

type Note struct {
	ID         idgen.ID
	NotebookID idgen.ID
	Title      string
	Body       string
	Visibility Visibility

	// Per-FIELD logical clocks. The merge rule is last-writer-wins per
	// field, so title and body each carry their own (lamport, actor)
	// pair. One timestamp for the whole row would make a title edit and
	// a body edit conflict when they do not (D11).
	TitleClock Clock
	BodyClock  Clock

	Version   int64 // optimistic concurrency for the REST path
	CreatedBy idgen.ID
	CreatedAt time.Time
	UpdatedAt time.Time
	DeletedAt *time.Time
}

func (n *Note) Deleted() bool { return n.DeletedAt != nil }

// Clock is a Lamport timestamp plus the actor that stamped it. The actor
// breaks ties deterministically, so two devices that write concurrently
// with the same counter still converge to the same answer.
type Clock struct {
	Lamport int64
	Actor   idgen.ID
}

// After reports whether c happened after other under the merge rule.
// Ties are broken by actor id, which is arbitrary but TOTAL — and total
// is the only property that matters, because every replica computes the
// same result.
func (c Clock) After(other Clock) bool {
	if c.Lamport != other.Lamport {
		return c.Lamport > other.Lamport
	}
	return c.Actor > other.Actor
}

// ---- rules ---------------------------------------------------------

func ValidateTitle(s string) error {
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(s) > MaxTitleRunes {
		return ErrTitleTooLong
	}
	if !utf8.ValidString(s) {
		return errors.New("title must be valid UTF-8")
	}
	return nil
}

func ValidateBody(s string) error {
	if len(s) > MaxBodyBytes {
		return ErrBodyTooLarge
	}
	if !utf8.ValidString(s) {
		return errors.New("body must be valid UTF-8")
	}
	return nil
}

// NormaliseTitle is applied on every write so that a title is stable
// regardless of which client produced it — otherwise a trailing space
// from one device and not another looks like a conflicting edit forever.
func NormaliseTitle(s string) string {
	s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\n", " ")
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(s) > MaxTitleRunes {
		r := []rune(s)
		s = string(r[:MaxTitleRunes])
	}
	return s
}

// Apply is THE merge rule, and it lives in the domain so the server, the
// sync path and the local client all use the same code. Returns whether
// the operation won.
func (n *Note) Apply(field string, value string, clk Clock) bool {
	switch field {
	case "title":
		if !clk.After(n.TitleClock) {
			return false
		}
		n.Title, n.TitleClock = NormaliseTitle(value), clk
	case "body":
		if !clk.After(n.BodyClock) {
			return false
		}
		n.Body, n.BodyClock = value, clk
	case "visibility":
		// Visibility is not a mergeable field: it is a permission change,
		// and a stale offline device must not be able to re-publish a
		// note the owner unpublished. It goes through the REST path with
		// an explicit version check instead.
		return false
	default:
		return false
	}
	n.UpdatedAt = time.Now()
	n.Version++
	return true
}
Why visibility is deliberately not mergeable

Every field that can be merged by last-writer-wins can be resurrected by a device that has been offline. For a title that is a minor annoyance; for a permission it is a security hole — a laptop that has been closed for three weeks, holding a stale “public” value with a high Lamport counter, would silently republish a note the owner made private. Permission-shaped fields therefore travel the explicit path with a version check and an authorization check, and the sync merge refuses them outright. The same reasoning applies to anything billing-related or anything another party relies on.

The queries

services/notes/query.sql
-- name: GetNoteForUser :one
-- Scoped by the caller in the QUERY, not checked in Go afterwards. This
-- is the structural defence against broken object-level authorization:
-- forgetting the scope returns nothing rather than someone else's note.
SELECT n.*
  FROM notes n
  JOIN notebooks nb ON nb.id = n.notebook_id
 WHERE n.id = @note_id
   AND n.deleted_at IS NULL
   AND nb.deleted_at IS NULL
   AND (
        nb.owner_id = @user_id
     OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM acl_replica a
                 WHERE a.notebook_id = nb.id AND a.user_id = @user_id)
   );

-- name: ListNotesPage :many
-- KEYSET pagination, not OFFSET. OFFSET 100000 makes Postgres read and
-- discard 100,000 rows; a keyset seeks straight to the position. It is
-- also stable under concurrent inserts, which OFFSET is not.
SELECT id, title, visibility, updated_at, version,
       left(body, 280) AS excerpt
  FROM notes
 WHERE notebook_id = @notebook_id
   AND deleted_at IS NULL
   AND (updated_at, id) < (@cursor_updated_at, @cursor_id)
 ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC
 LIMIT @page_size;

-- name: InsertNote :one
INSERT INTO notes (
    id, notebook_id, title, body, visibility,
    title_lamport, title_actor, body_lamport, body_actor,
    created_by
) VALUES (
    @id, @notebook_id, @title, @body, @visibility,
    @lamport, @actor, @lamport, @actor,
    @created_by
)
RETURNING *;

-- name: UpdateNoteChecked :one
-- Optimistic concurrency: the update only applies if the caller's
-- version is still current. RowsAffected = 0 means someone else wrote
-- first, and the caller gets a 409 with the current state to merge.
UPDATE notes
   SET title         = coalesce(sqlc.narg('title'),      title),
       body          = coalesce(sqlc.narg('body'),       body),
       visibility    = coalesce(sqlc.narg('visibility'), visibility),
       title_lamport = CASE WHEN sqlc.narg('title') IS NOT NULL
                            THEN @lamport ELSE title_lamport END,
       title_actor   = CASE WHEN sqlc.narg('title') IS NOT NULL
                            THEN @actor   ELSE title_actor   END,
       body_lamport  = CASE WHEN sqlc.narg('body') IS NOT NULL
                            THEN @lamport ELSE body_lamport  END,
       body_actor    = CASE WHEN sqlc.narg('body') IS NOT NULL
                            THEN @actor   ELSE body_actor    END,
       version    = version + 1,
       updated_at = now()
 WHERE id = @id
   AND version = @expected_version
   AND deleted_at IS NULL
RETURNING *;

-- name: SoftDeleteNote :execrows
-- A tombstone, never a DELETE. An offline client must be able to learn
-- that a note was removed; a vanished row is indistinguishable from a
-- note it has not synced yet.
UPDATE notes SET deleted_at = now(), version = version + 1
 WHERE id = @id AND deleted_at IS NULL;

-- name: PurgeDeletedNotes :execrows
-- Run weekly. Tombstones are only needed until every client has had a
-- chance to see them; 90 days is far more than enough and keeps the
-- table from growing without bound.
DELETE FROM notes
 WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at < now() - interval '90 days';

-- name: GetRole :one
-- The ACL replica lookup: one index hit, no network call (D10).
SELECT role FROM acl_replica
 WHERE notebook_id = @notebook_id AND user_id = @user_id;
Keyset pagination, and the tie-breaker that makes it correct

Ordering by updated_at alone is not stable: two notes updated in the same millisecond can swap places between pages, so one is shown twice and another never. Adding the id as a secondary key makes the ordering total, and the row-value comparison (updated_at, id) < (…, …) expresses “strictly before this position” in a form Postgres can satisfy from the index in one seek. The cursor handed to the client is those two values, base64-encoded so it reads as opaque and nobody builds logic on its contents.

The store

services/notes/internal/store/store.go
// Package store is the Postgres adapter. It is the ONLY package in this
// service that imports pgx, and it translates every driver error into a
// domain error on the way out (B08).
package store

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/idgen"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/pg"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/notes/internal/domain"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/notes/internal/store/db" // sqlc output
)

type Store struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
	q    *db.Queries
}

// Compile-time conformance: if the app package's interface gains a
// method, this file fails to build with a precise message (L06).
var _ domain.Repository = (*Store)(nil)

func New(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Store {
	return &Store{pool: pool, q: db.New(pool)}
}

func (s *Store) GetNote(ctx context.Context, userID, noteID idgen.ID) (*domain.Note, error) {
	row, err := s.q.GetNoteForUser(ctx, db.GetNoteForUserParams{
		NoteID: noteID, UserID: userID,
	})
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			// The same error whether the note does not exist or the
			// caller may not see it. Distinguishing them turns the
			// endpoint into an existence oracle for other people's ids.
			return nil, domain.ErrNotFound
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("get note %s: %w", noteID, err)
	}
	return toDomain(row), nil
}

func (s *Store) UpdateNote(ctx context.Context, in domain.UpdateInput) (*domain.Note, error) {
	row, err := s.q.UpdateNoteChecked(ctx, db.UpdateNoteCheckedParams{
		ID: in.NoteID, ExpectedVersion: in.ExpectedVersion,
		Title: in.Title, Body: in.Body, Visibility: in.Visibility,
		Lamport: in.Clock.Lamport, Actor: in.Clock.Actor,
	})
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			// No row matched: either the note is gone, or the version
			// moved. Disambiguate with a second read so the caller can
			// return 404 or 409 correctly.
			if _, gerr := s.GetNote(ctx, in.UserID, in.NoteID); gerr != nil {
				return nil, domain.ErrNotFound
			}
			return nil, domain.ErrVersionStale
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("update note %s: %w", in.NoteID, err)
	}
	return toDomain(row), nil
}

// toDomain is the boundary. Nothing above this package ever sees a db.*
// type, which is what lets the schema change without touching the
// domain and what makes an in-memory fake possible.
func toDomain(r db.Note) *domain.Note {
	n := &domain.Note{
		ID: r.ID, NotebookID: r.NotebookID,
		Title: r.Title, Body: r.Body,
		Visibility: domain.Visibility(r.Visibility),
		TitleClock: domain.Clock{Lamport: r.TitleLamport, Actor: r.TitleActor},
		BodyClock:  domain.Clock{Lamport: r.BodyLamport, Actor: r.BodyActor},
		Version:    r.Version, CreatedBy: r.CreatedBy,
		CreatedAt: r.CreatedAt, UpdatedAt: r.UpdatedAt,
	}
	if r.DeletedAt.Valid {
		t := r.DeletedAt.Time
		n.DeletedAt = &t
	}
	return n
}

The write path: a row update and an op, atomically

services/notes/internal/app/notes.go
package app

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/idgen"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/outbox"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/pg"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/notes/internal/domain"
)

type UpdateNoteInput struct {
	UserID          idgen.ID
	DeviceID        idgen.ID
	NoteID          idgen.ID
	Title           *string // nil means "leave alone" — not "set to empty" (B03)
	Body            *string
	ExpectedVersion int64
}

// UpdateNote is the REST write path. Every mutation here ALSO appends to
// the operation log, so a note edited from the web is indistinguishable
// from one edited offline as far as sync is concerned. Forgetting this
// is the bug that makes web edits invisible to desktop clients.
func (s *Service) UpdateNote(ctx context.Context, in UpdateNoteInput) (*domain.Note, error) {
	if in.Title != nil {
		if err := domain.ValidateTitle(*in.Title); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	if in.Body != nil {
		if err := domain.ValidateBody(*in.Body); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	var out *domain.Note

	err := pg.InTxAs(ctx, s.pool, in.UserID.String(), func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		q := s.q.WithTx(tx)

		note, err := q.GetNoteForUpdate(ctx, in.NoteID)
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			return domain.ErrNotFound
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// Authorization against the local ACL replica: one index lookup,
		// no network hop (D10).
		role, err := s.roleFor(ctx, q, note.NotebookID, in.UserID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if !role.CanWrite() {
			return domain.ErrForbidden
		}

		// One Lamport tick per transaction, shared by every field touched
		// here, so a simultaneous title-and-body edit is one logical
		// event rather than two that can interleave.
		seq, err := q.NextSeq(ctx, note.NotebookID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		clk := domain.Clock{Lamport: seq, Actor: in.UserID}

		updated, err := q.UpdateNoteChecked(ctx, /* ...params... */)
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			return domain.ErrVersionStale
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// Append one op per changed field. The op log is what every
		// other device pulls, so this is not bookkeeping — it IS the
		// mechanism by which the edit reaches anyone else.
		for _, f := range changedFields(in) {
			if err := q.InsertOp(ctx, InsertOpParams{
				OpID:       idgen.New(), // server-generated for REST writes
				NotebookID: note.NotebookID, NoteID: in.NoteID,
				ServerSeq: seq, ActorID: in.UserID, DeviceID: in.DeviceID,
				Kind: "set_field", Field: f.name, Value: f.value,
				Lamport: clk.Lamport, Applied: true,
			}); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}

		// The realtime doorbell, published through the outbox so it
		// cannot be sent for a transaction that then rolls back (B12).
		if _, err := outbox.Enqueue(ctx, tx, "notes.changed", NotesChanged{
			NotebookID: note.NotebookID, NoteID: in.NoteID,
			ServerSeq: seq, ActorID: in.UserID, DeviceID: in.DeviceID,
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		out = toDomain(updated)
		return nil
	})
	return out, err
}
services/notes/query.sql — the sequence allocator
-- name: NextSeq :one
-- One counter PER NOTEBOOK, so two notebooks never contend and a busy
-- notebook cannot stall a quiet one. A global bigserial would serialise
-- every write in the service through a single sequence.
--
-- This is a row lock held for the rest of the transaction, which is
-- exactly what we want: writes to one notebook are totally ordered, and
-- that total order is what the whole sync protocol rests on (D11).
INSERT INTO notebook_seq (notebook_id, last_seq)
VALUES (@notebook_id, 1)
ON CONFLICT (notebook_id) DO UPDATE
   SET last_seq = notebook_seq.last_seq + 1
RETURNING last_seq;

-- name: InsertOp :exec
-- ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the client-generated op_id is the entire
-- idempotency mechanism for push: a retried batch inserts nothing the
-- second time, and the client still gets a success (D12).
INSERT INTO note_ops (
    op_id, notebook_id, note_id, server_seq, actor_id, device_id,
    kind, field, value, lamport, applied
) VALUES (
    @op_id, @notebook_id, @note_id, @server_seq, @actor_id, @device_id,
    @kind, @field, @value, @lamport, @applied
)
ON CONFLICT (op_id) DO NOTHING;
The per-notebook sequence is a lock, and that is intentional

ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on notebook_seq takes a row lock held until the transaction commits, so concurrent writes to the same notebook serialise. That is the price of a total order — and a total order is what lets a client say “give me everything after 8791” and be certain it has missed nothing. The cost is bounded because the lock is per notebook and the transaction is short; the thing to avoid is doing any network I/O inside it (B07). If a single notebook ever becomes hot enough for this to matter, the answer is to shard by note rather than to weaken the ordering.

Creating a notebook, and the event that makes it shareable

services/notes/internal/app/notebooks.go
package app

func (s *Service) CreateNotebook(ctx context.Context, userID idgen.ID,
	title string) (*domain.Notebook, error) {

	if err := domain.ValidateTitle(title); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	nbID := idgen.New()
	var out *domain.Notebook

	err := pg.InTx(ctx, s.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		q := s.q.WithTx(tx)

		nb, err := q.InsertNotebook(ctx, InsertNotebookParams{
			ID: nbID, OwnerID: userID, Title: domain.NormaliseTitle(title),
		})
		if err != nil {
			return pg.Translate(err)
		}

		// Seed the ACL replica with the owner immediately. Waiting for
		// collab's event would leave a window in which the creator
		// cannot read their own notebook — a race that shows up as
		// "sometimes a new notebook 404s right after creation".
		if err := q.UpsertACL(ctx, UpsertACLParams{
			NotebookID: nbID, UserID: userID,
			Role: string(domain.RoleOwner), Revision: 0,
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if err := q.InitSeq(ctx, nbID); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// collab is the source of truth for permissions, so it must
		// learn about the owner. It is an event, not a call: notebook
		// creation must not fail because collab is restarting.
		_, err = outbox.Enqueue(ctx, tx, "notes.notebook_created",
			NotebookCreated{NotebookID: nbID, OwnerID: userID, Title: title})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		out = toDomainNotebook(nb)
		return nil
	})
	return out, err
}
Seed locally, then reconcile — do not wait for the round trip

The owner row is written into the local ACL replica in the same transaction that creates the notebook, and also published to collab. That is deliberate duplication: the local write removes a user-visible race, and the event makes collab authoritative. A nightly reconciliation job compares the replica against collab's memberships and reports divergence, which is the honest way to run an eventually-consistent read model — you accept the window, you make it small, and you measure it rather than assuming it is zero.

The HTTP layer

services/notes/internal/transport/http/notes.go
package http

import (
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/httpx"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/problem"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/validate"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/notes/internal/app"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/notes/internal/domain"
)

type updateNoteRequest struct {
	// Pointers distinguish "absent" from "set to empty" — a plain string
	// field cannot express "leave the title alone" (B03).
	Title *string `json:"title"`
	Body  *string `json:"body"`
}

func (r updateNoteRequest) Validate() *problem.Problem {
	v := validate.New()
	if r.Title == nil && r.Body == nil {
		v.Custom(false, "body", "empty_patch", "supply at least one field")
	}
	if r.Title != nil {
		v.Length("title", *r.Title, 0, domain.MaxTitleRunes).UTF8("title", *r.Title)
	}
	if r.Body != nil {
		v.Custom(len(*r.Body) <= domain.MaxBodyBytes, "body", "too_large",
			"must be at most 1 MiB").UTF8("body", *r.Body)
	}
	return v.Problem()
}

func (h *Handler) updateNote(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	ctx := r.Context()
	sub := httpx.MustSubject(ctx)

	noteID, err := idgen.Parse(r.PathValue("id"))
	if err != nil {
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.BadRequest("malformed note id"))
		return
	}

	req, p := httpx.Decode[updateNoteRequest](w, r)
	if p != nil {
		problem.Write(ctx, w, p)
		return
	}
	if p := req.Validate(); p != nil {
		problem.Write(ctx, w, p)
		return
	}

	// Optimistic concurrency over HTTP uses If-Match with the version as
	// an ETag — the standard mechanism, so caches and clients understand
	// it without documentation.
	version, p := parseIfMatch(r)
	if p != nil {
		problem.Write(ctx, w, p)
		return
	}

	note, err := h.app.UpdateNote(ctx, app.UpdateNoteInput{
		UserID: sub.UserID, DeviceID: deviceFrom(r),
		NoteID: noteID, Title: req.Title, Body: req.Body,
		ExpectedVersion: version,
	})
	if err != nil {
		h.writeError(w, r, err)
		return
	}

	w.Header().Set("ETag", strconv.FormatInt(note.Version, 10))
	httpx.JSON(ctx, w, http.StatusOK, toResponse(note))
}

// toResponse is the wire type. It is SEPARATE from domain.Note on
// purpose: adding a field to the domain must not silently publish it,
// and renaming a column must not break every client (B03).
type noteResponse struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	NotebookID string `json:"notebook_id"`
	Title      string `json:"title"`
	Body       string `json:"body"`
	Visibility string `json:"visibility"`
	Version    int64  `json:"version"`
	UpdatedAt  string `json:"updated_at"`
}

func (h *Handler) writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
	ctx := r.Context()
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, domain.ErrNotFound):
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.NotFound("note"))
	case errors.Is(err, domain.ErrForbidden):
		// 403, and the body says nothing about whether the note exists.
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Forbidden("you do not have write access"))
	case errors.Is(err, domain.ErrVersionStale):
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.New(http.StatusPreconditionFailed,
			"version-conflict", "Note was modified",
			"reload and reapply your change"))
	case errors.Is(err, domain.ErrBodyTooLarge), errors.Is(err, domain.ErrTitleTooLong):
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Validation(nil))
	case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
		return
	default:
		h.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "notes", "err", err, "route", r.Pattern)
		problem.Write(ctx, w, problem.Internal())
	}
}
Interview follow-up

“How do you handle two users editing the same record at once?” Name the two mechanisms and when each applies. For a connected client, optimistic concurrency: a version column, If-Match on the request, and a 412 with the current state so the user can reapply — which surfaces the conflict to a human who can resolve it. For an offline client there is nobody to ask at the time of the write, so you need a deterministic merge rule instead: per-field last-writer-wins with a logical clock and a total tie-break, plus an explicit decision about which fields are not mergeable. The fields you exclude — permissions, money, anything another party relies on — are the interesting part of the answer.

D08

Public notes, search and caching

Publishing a note moves it from an authenticated API to the open internet, which changes the threat model completely: untrusted markdown becomes HTML in a browser, an unguessable slug becomes the only access control, and a cache that gets this wrong serves one user's note to another.

Publishing

services/notes/internal/app/publish.go
package app

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/base32"
	"errors"
	"strings"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"

	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/outbox"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/platform/pg"
	"github.com/quillhq/quill/services/notes/internal/domain"
)

type PublishInput struct {
	UserID   idgen.ID
	NoteID   idgen.ID
	Password string // optional: a second factor on the link
}

func (s *Service) Publish(ctx context.Context, in PublishInput) (string, error) {
	var slug string

	err := pg.InTx(ctx, s.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		q := s.q.WithTx(tx)

		note, err := q.GetNoteForUpdate(ctx, in.NoteID)
		if errors.Is(pg.Translate(err), pg.ErrNotFound) {
			return domain.ErrNotFound
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// Publishing is an OWNER action. An editor can write the note but
		// cannot decide to expose it to the internet — that asymmetry is
